issues.detail: The Greek 'εχε' (echē) is an imperative meaning 'have' or 'hold', but the Vietnamese 'giữ lấy' (keep/hold onto) combined with the structure 'cho chính mình' (for yourself) slightly shifts the nuance of the command to 'keep it for yourself' rather than the direct imperative 'have [it]'. However, the more significant issue is the final clause.

The Greek 'εν ω δοκιμαζει' (en hō dokimazei) means 'in which he tests/proves [himself]'. The Vietnamese 'trong việc mình chấp nhận' translates to 'in the matter one accepts'. 'Chấp nhận' (accept) is not a faithful rendering of 'δοκιμάζει' (test/prove/examine).
